title: What State Is Your Country In?
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（社会服务与人际沟通·国家构成与公民权利）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（社会服务与人际沟通·国家构成与公民权利）　|　核心词汇：state　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 state 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In my first civics lesson our teacher wrote one word on the board: ① state. 'A state,' she said, 'is not a building. It is an agreement between millions of people who will never meet.' I remember thinking that it sounded like a dictionary definition rather than something I could see.

Then she asked us to look out of the window. Across the road stood a ② state school, built with tax money and open to every child in the district. 'That building is the state in concrete form,' she said. 'So is the hospital. So is the bus that takes you home.'

That month we visited a ③ state-owned power plant on the edge of the city. Our guide ④ stated that the plant supplied nearly a third of the province's electricity. Then he read us a page of the constitution, which ⑤ states that every citizen has the right to education and to safe working conditions.

On the bus home I sat beside a girl from another town. Her town, she said, was in a poor ⑥ state: the library had closed, the swimming pool had been sold, and the young people were leaving. In her country, she added, a ⑦ state can decide its own school rules, so a town like hers could raise the school-leaving age if it wished. 'People keep saying the state should do something,' she said. 'I now know it means someone must pay tax and someone must decide.'

I began to keep a notebook of what I actually see: a repaired road, a new bus stop, a ⑧ state-funded reading room for left-behind children. None of it is dramatic. But each of these things is the agreement being kept.

' ⑨ The state is us,' our teacher said at the end of term, 'and it must protect the weakest among us, or the agreement means nothing.' Then she asked us one question: 'What ⑩ state is your country in?' Not a score, not a speech — something each of us has to answer with what we do.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: C. n. 州；邦（联邦制国家的行政区）
D. adj. 国家提供的；公立的（state school / state-funded）
E. adj. 国家的；国有的（state-owned / state visit）
F. v. 陈述；说明（口头或书面表达）
G. v. （宪法、文件）规定；载明
H. 固定搭配：in a poor / good state 状况不佳 / 良好

items.q: wrote one word on the board: state
a state school, built with tax money
Our guide stated that the plant supplied
the constitution, which states that every citizen
a state can decide its own school rules
What state is your country in?

answers.why: 老师给的定义是“几百万人之间的约定”，指政治意义上的“国家”，取名词“国家；政府”。
state school 指用税收办的“公立学校”，state 作定语，取形容词义“国家提供的”。
state-owned 意为“国有的”，指国有发电厂，与 state school 都属于 state + 分词构成的定语。
guide 作主语，stated that 后接宾语从句，是“陈述、说明”这一动作，取动词义。
主语是 constitution（宪法），后接 that 从句说明其内容，取“（文件）规定；载明”，比 ④ 更正式。
in a poor state 是固定搭配，指小镇“状况不佳”，后文关馆、卖泳池是具体表现。
In her country 之后谈地方可以自定校规，指联邦制国家里的“州；邦”，取行政区义。
state-funded 意为“国家资助的”，修饰 reading room，与 state school 同属形容词用法。
与前文“国家是人与人的约定”呼应，The state is us 中的 state 仍指“国家”。
What state is your country in? 问的是“处于什么状况”，取名词“状态；状况”，与 in a poor state 同源。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 这所学校是公立的，每个孩子都可以免费上学。（state school）
这家国有企业为全省提供电力。（state-owned）
宪法规定，每个公民都有受教育的权利。（states）
那个镇的图书馆关了，整座镇子状况很糟。（in a poor state）
向导向我们说明，这座工厂供应全省近三分之一的电力。（stated that）
你所在的城市现在处于什么状况？（state）
answers: This is a state school, and every child can study here for free.
This state-owned company supplies electricity to the whole province.
The constitution states that every citizen has the right to education.
The library in that town has closed, and the whole town is in a poor state.
The guide stated that the plant supplied nearly a third of the province's electricity.
What state is your city in now?

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 state 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: A state is not a flag on a map but an agreement between citizens.
The government has stated that every child in the county may attend a state school.
The constitution states that national rights belong to every citizen, not only to officials.
Our town was in a poor state ten years ago, when nearly half of the population had left.
With tax money the state has built a state-funded library and a new road.
A republic stays strong only when its citizens care about the state of their own community.
